newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Pemex details 1996 crude, natgas output.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Pemex details 1996 crude, natgas output.

text.p: Mexico's state oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) in 1996 saw a 10 percent increase in crude output in its offshore region to an average 2.13 million barrels per day (bpd), the company said in a statement Thursday.
Pemex's largest production increase was in the offshore region, Pemex's greatest source of crude. The company is working to further increase output in the area with extensive 1997 drilling projects.
In Pemex's southern drilling region, output grew 7.88 percent to 630,000 bpd. Production reached 96,000 bpd in the northern region, from 1995's average 95,000 bpd.
Of a total 2.86 million bpd of crude, 1.37 million bpd was of Pemex's heavy Maya brand, 910,000 bpd was the company's light Isthmus and the remaining 578,000 bpd composed of extra-light Olmeca crude.
In natural gas, Pemex said its 1996 output of 4.195 billion cubic feet per day (cfd) was divided into 3.478 billion cfd associated gas, and the remainder non-associated gas.
In the southern region Pemex extracted 1.99 billion cfd. The company reported production of 1.563 billion cfd in the offshore region and 643 million cfd in the northern region.
